analysis.title: Macro Derivs Flow: Large positioning unwinds / Surge in Rates call options / $CNH downside
key_insights: Week's flows were dominated by positioning-driven equity unwinds, with UBS PB deleveraging indicators flashing red across regions.
Tech selling is now led by Hyperscalers rather than Semis as in prior weeks. There was small net buying in Memory and Tech Hardware, where positioning was already low.
Many of the incremental shorts added on the PB desk are in AI Tech names, which UBS describes as new.
AI Industrials also saw selling pressure, while defensive sectors saw buying (some of it short covering): Healthcare, Defense, Packaging, Staples.
After the squeeze higher in Staples, there were multiple XLP downside trades looking to fade the move.
AI unwinds also hit Japan and Taiwan. Japan continues to see large, persistent hedge fund degrossing, led by Tech.

Korea Tech was also sold but at much smaller magnitude than prior weeks. Korea Memory flows were mixed (buying Samsung Electronics, selling Hynix), which UBS reads as positioning already having been reduced.
China Internet names kept seeing selling on cash pad despite already very low positioning, led by names with elevated AI capex spend.

China onshore was under pressure, prompting more National Team buying. Late in the week CSI call option trades picked up, mainly on CSI300, which is more defensive, has elevated outperformance levels and low vols.
FX saw some spill-over from risk-off: USD-upside demand, EUR selling and CHF buying, plus buying of GBP and AUD over the week.
USDCNH downside was a persistent trade, with demand through the week for downside digits and put spreads to play continued yuan appreciation.
The rates reaction was much more acute than in FX. Thursday's move drove a surge in outright Treasury calls, with skew shifting significantly toward calls.

There was heavy demand for USD front-end upside, preferring call spreads, which UBS reads as looking for a moderate unwind of Fed hikes priced in. In the back end, investors were more willing to position for a potentially large rates rally.
Europe rates flows were mixed, with both downside and upside EURIBOR trades, which UBS says reflects continued fiscal concerns.

Brazil equity flows turned slightly more cautious ahead of Sunday's 2nd round, with some trimming of longs and unwinds of EWZ upside. Clients were generally willing to keep upside positioning despite the strong rally and close polling.
